$$ \frac{p(759x)}{759x} \equiv \frac{p(x)}{x} \pmod{1009} \implies p(759x) \equiv 759 \cdot p(x) \pmod{1009} $$
Let $p(X) = \sum_{j=0}^{19} c_j X^j$. For the above condition to hold for all $x$, the coefficients must satisfy:
$$ c_j (759)^j \equiv c_j \cdot 759 \pmod{1009} $$
For any non-zero coefficient $c_j$, we require $759^{j-1} \equiv 1 \pmod{1009}$.
Since $759$ has a multiplicative order of exactly $9$ modulo $1009$ (as indicated by the "nine-point" hint and verifying $759^9 \equiv 1 \pmod{1009}$), $j-1$ must be a multiple of 9. Within the degree bound $K < 20$, the only possible degrees $j$ are 1, 10, and 19.

$$ p(X) = c_1 X + c_{10} X^{10} + c_{19} X^{19} $$
